title: Black Hole Recordings New Releases – Week 41
excerpt: Find the latest electronic music news, features, interviews, videos and podcasts from Beatportal - the reference for DJs and dance music artists.
content:
A selection of this week’s standout releases across the dancefloor.

This week moves between different shades of electronic music, with familiar trance influences meeting newer production ideas, softer moments sitting alongside heavier grooves, and plenty of melody along the way. There’s a good mix of nostalgia and fresh energy here, with each release bringing its own little twist to the week.

Push - Open The Night [Black Hole Recordings]

Push opens a slightly different chapter with “Open The Night,” bringing emotional vocals and a more ecstatic feel into his 140 BPM sound. But despite the tempo, speed isn’t really the point here. The production keeps things focused on a strong groove, driving energy, and Eli Hayes’ vocal hooks, giving it a straightforward, uplifting feel without overcomplicating the arrangement.

After a busy summer of touring and working from my remote studio in Belgium, I’ve been spending a lot of time in the studio again working on new music, exploring a more euphoric side again than I was known for. ‘Open The Night’ was born out of that process.

— Push

Orjan Nilsen - If There's A Chance [Black Hole Recordings]

Orjan Nilsen brings back the Balearic side of trance with “If There’s A Chance,” a progressive-leaning cut built around warm synths, a lovely guitar line, and the kind of melody that doesn’t need to rush to make an impact. It follows his successful “Sankthansaften,” continuing that same sun-soaked, emotional direction while giving it a fresh setting.

At a time when rave and UKG influences are everywhere, Orjan goes in the opposite direction, stripping things back to the melodies, beauty, and emotion at the heart of trance. “If There’s A Chance” feels like a reminder of just how powerful that side of the genre can be.

Hensha x YORK x DuMonde - The Curtain [Black Hole Recordings]

Some trance tracks just refuse to disappear. “The Curtain” was born when Hensha was finding his way as a producer and experimenting with the sounds that first pulled him into trance. The track later became one of the classics featured on ‘In Search Of Sunrise 7’ compilation, and almost two decades later, it got a new life as Hensha x YORK x DuMonde, bringing its euphoric melodies and emotional character back into focus.

The idea for ‘The Curtain’ came in 2007, when I was fascinated by the trance scene and artists like Tiësto, Ferry Corsten and Activa. As a new producer, I wanted to find my own approach, adding church choruses and an emotional melody. Now, together with YORK and DuMonde, we’ve brought the track back to its roots while giving it a fresh, modern sound.

 — Hensha

RAM & Bogdan Vix – Umami [In Trance We Trust]

Originally released on Nocturnal Knights a couple of years ago, “Umami” gets a slightly reworked version for In Trance We Trust, with RAM teaming up with Bogdan Vix. The new version keeps the track’s bright melodic hooks and soaring peaks, while leaning further into the old-school trance character that has always been part of the In Trance We Trust identity.

With its sweeping melodies and a real sense of lift and an unmistakable RAM touch, “Umami” feels right at home on a label with almost 30 years of history behind it.

JES – Dreamer [Magik Muzik]

JES looks at what it really means to keep chasing a dream with “Dreamer,” a housy, vocal-driven track that balances the excitement of wanting something badly with the doubts that inevitably come with it. It’s less about the perfect version of the dream and more about what happens after years of pursuing it — the wrong turns, second-guessing, and that feeling that still tells you to keep going.

“Dreamer” also gives us an early glimpse of JES’ upcoming album, due in November, where this idea of holding on to that drive continues to run through the music.

Dreaming isn’t always magical. Sometimes it’s messy, uncertain, and a little insane. Years later, the dream is still here, along with the doubts and the obstacles that life throws at you. But even when I’m questioning everything, there’s still something in me that screams, go. That unrelenting energy is the heart of ‘Dreamer,’ and the inspiration for my new album.

— JES

Phillip Castle - Forever [You & Me] [Magik Muzik]

Phillip Castle turns his own love story into “Forever,” a progressive trance gem filled with bright melodies, catchy vocals, and feel-good energy. Written for his wife Anna, the track goes back to that first meeting, the kind of moment when you barely know someone yet, but something just clicks, and you already have a feeling they’re going to stay in your life.

The arrangement blends modern and nostalgic trance, reflecting Phillip’s own relationship: moving forward together while still remembering and honouring the moments that brought them here.

Raffi Habel, Artichokes & KXNE - Lost & Found [Force Of Habit]

Raffi Habel, Artichokes and KXNE team up for ‘Lost & Found,’ an interesting house project released as an EP with both a Club Mix and an Acid Club Mix. Sitting between bass house and tech house, the two versions play with the same idea from slightly different angles, combining a heavy low end with sharp grooves and a touch of acid.
